To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lactate dehydrogenas and malate dehyrogenase activities and isozymes patterns of maturing rat Sertoli cells increase between the second and third weeks of age and that lactate dehydrogeanase isozyme complement includes all five isozyme and, in the most mature rats, has a shift toward the isozymes rich in subunit.
lactate and pyruvate are produced by Sertoli cells and that their production increases during the maturing period of these cells.
lactate and malate dehydorgenase activities increase in maturing Sertolli cells, and that lactate dehydrogenases isozyme complement includes all five isozymic forms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the lactate dehydrogenases and malate dehydorgenases in Sertoli cells, in particular with their isozyme patterns and activities.
the study of the metabolism of Sertoli cell and, more precisely, with lactate and pyruvate metabolism in the seminifereous epithelium.
the study of the metabolic activity of the Sertoli cell, the main component of the seminiferus epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LDH is an important enzyme of Sertoli cell metabolism, and that it is a marker of Sertoli maturation.
LDH and MDH are involved in the metabolism of the seminiferic epithelium and are important for the maturing process of the seminifieric epithelium.

the changes in LDH and MDH activities and isozymic patterns of maturing cultured Sertoli cells are consistent with the hypothesis of an increasing production of pyruvate/lactate and of a finer regulation of their production during the maturing process of Sertoli cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lactate and pyruvate, which are produced in large amounts by the Sertoli cell, are the main energy substrates for the germ cell.
Sertoli cells are able to synthesize lactate and malate from glucose and, in the process of maturation, they become able to produce more lactate and malic acid.
the maturing Sertol cells are able to produce lactate/pyruvaate and malate in a finely regulated manner, which is consistent with their nutritional role in spermatogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lactate is the primary source of energy for spermatogenesis and the Sertoli cell is the primary producer of lactate.

LDH isozymes in Sertoli cells are differentially regulated during the maturation of the seminiferus tubules, and that lactate/pyruate are important energy sources for spermatogenic cells in the seminiferos epithelium.
the Sertoli cells are not only responsible for the nutrition of the germ cells, but also play an important role in the metabolism of the testis.
